So I re-opened and confirmed every reported figure that feeds my fair value at source: the Q2 8-K, the 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, and the June 5 and Aug 10 8-Ks. The only company releases are the Oct 6 Constellation PPA (890 MW of uprates, 20 years; a separate 2,700 MW, 15-year supply deal; first uprate 2028; cost undisclosed) and the Sep 30/Oct 1 Gemini 4 Argon preview (Fairwind-only, no GA date). I also built the 10-peer comp set my prior file lacked, on one CY2027 basis. Its median is 19.6x P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA; GOOGL is at 23.0x all-in and 22.0x core. agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. This is somewhat tighter than the 32% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the Mar-May 2026 re-rating (weekly close $274 in late March to a $408.61 high in May) [43], and wider than base-rate large-cap moves only in the left tail. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and statistics endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus comes from MarketScreener and StockAnalysis.
